experiment_b.reason: Round 2 showed that 3 replicas add only about 1.25x throughput (0.111-0.113 vs 0.087-0.091 req/s) on the shared Mac CPUs, and one pod already saturates its 2-CPU quota. k8s/hpa.yaml is included in the repo, but its autoscaling behaviour was not measured.

notes.generator_changes: Round 2 load generator: 1 s back-off after any failed request; 503s counted separately from other errors; every exception recorded with its type; one final record per client; possible_sleep flag per cell. Round 1 had none of these.
notes.a-r1-c1: The cell started 2 s after scaling from 3 replicas to 1; the first request was routed to a departing pod and failed after 38.8 s ('No route to host'). The recorded 0.053 req/s is a driver artifact. Recomputation (not a recorded value): 5 OK requests over 55.1 s from the first OK start to the last OK end = 0.091 req/s (same as 1 / mean OK latency of 11.0 s). An earlier rough estimate of 0.094 used only the 10.5-10.7 s requests.
notes.a-r1-c6: possible_sleep=True is a false positive: completions were steady every 11-12 s (largest gap 11.9 s); the 150 s wall time includes the six queued requests draining after the 90 s deadline.

known_tool_gaps: The driver waits for the remaining pods to be Ready after scaling, but not for departing pods to leave the Service, so the first request of a cell right after a scale-down can hit a terminating pod (a-r1-c1).

The possible_sleep wall-time rule (> 1.5 x duration) counts queue drain after the deadline, so cells with a deep queue (1 replica, 6 clients) are flagged even without a pause; the completion-gap rule is the reliable signal there.
